21.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, set thy face toward Jerusalem, and drop thy word toward the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel, 3 And say to the land of Israel, Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I am against thee, and will draw forth my sword out of his sheath, and will cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked. 4 Seeing then that I will cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked, therefore shall my sword go forth out of his sheath against all flesh from the south to the north: 5 That all flesh may know that I the LORD have drawn forth my sword out of his sheath: it shall not return any more. 6 Sigh therefore, thou son of man, with the breaking of thy loins; and with bitterness sigh before their eyes. 7 And it shall be, when they say unto thee, Wherefore sighest thou? that thou shalt answer, For the tidings; because it cometh: and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water: behold, it cometh, and shall be brought to pass, saith the Lord GOD."

21.0.1.en: He asked him to direct his gaze toward Jerusalem [1] and to prophesy openly against the holy land, the holy city and the holy Temple.

21.1.0.en: He who had previously stood interceding for them and pleading on their behalf in more than one place (Ezek 9:8) is now called to proclaim the judgments of God which come upon Israel, who declared her rejection of the commandment and her deliberate stubbornness. He speaks the words of the Lord, saying: "Behold, I am against thee, and will draw forth my sword out of his sheath, and will cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked" [3]. Since these matters are no longer in the eyes of the Lord, He sends His sword upon her and stands against her, and cuts off from her the righteous and the wicked. This does not mean here that He kills both without distinction between them, but He removes the righteous from her to transfer him to the land of the Chaldeans like the good figs (Jer 24), and removes the wicked by killing him in Judah, so the land loses both, through captivity and the sword. The Lord made clear His attitude toward the good figs in the Book of Jeremiah as follows: "Like these good figs, so will I acknowledge them that are carried away captive of Judah, whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans for their good. For I will set mine eyes upon them for good, and I will bring them again to this land: and I will build them, and not pull them down; and I will plant them, and not pluck them up. And I will give them an heart to know me, that I am the LORD: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: for they shall return unto me with their whole heart" (Jer 24:5-7). Thus He cuts off the good figs and the bad from Jerusalem, but separates the one from the other.

21.2.0.en: He asked him to sigh bitterly in public so that they would ask him the reason for his sighing, and he would answer openly, "For the tidings; because it cometh: and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water: behold, it cometh, and shall be brought to pass" [7]. God is not giving a parable but true tidings and a coming reality at which all tremble!

21.3.0.en: 8 Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 9 "Son of man, prophesy, and say, Thus saith the LORD; Say, A sword, a sword is sharpened, and also furbished: 10 It is sharpened to make a sore slaughter; it is furbished that it may glitter: should we then make mirth? it contemneth the rod of my son, as every tree. 11 And he hath given it to be furbished, that it may be handled: this sword is sharpened, and it is furbished, to give it into the hand of the slayer. 12 Cry and howl, son of man: for it shall be upon my people, it shall be upon all the princes of Israel: terrors by reason of the sword shall be upon my people: smite therefore upon thy thigh. 13 Because it is a trial, and what if the sword contemn even the rod? it shall be no more, saith the Lord GOD. 14 Thou therefore, son of man, prophesy, and smite thine hands together, and let the sword be doubled the third time, the sword of the slain: it is the sword of the great men that are slain, which entereth into their privy chambers. 15 I have set the point of the sword against all their gates, that their heart may faint, and their ruins be multiplied: ah! it is made bright, it is wrapped up for the slaughter. 16 Go thee one way or other, either on the right hand, or on the left, whithersoever thy face is set. 17 I will also smite mine hands together, and I will cause my fury to rest: I the LORD have said it."

21.4.0.en: This fearsome sword is in truth not the sword of Nebuchadnezzar but the sword of God Himself, who uses this king for discipline. It does its part well, for it is furbished and sharp, slaying the princes of Judah and the people, a great deadly sword, which is waved once, then a second time, then a third. It comes the first time after the verbal warning, the second time after the prophet smites upon his thigh [12], and the third time after he smites hand against hand [14], as though the going forth of the sword were not an end in itself, but goes forth when the leaders and the people reject God's warnings.

21.4.1.en: It is observed that it is a sharp sword that kills the wicked, but for the children of God it is "the rod of discipline" which slays in them the green tree (pagan worship) and not their souls, for He says of it: "it contemneth the rod of my son, as every tree" [10], and not every soul. It comes to destroy evil and sin, not sinners. It is a sword of trial [13] or a rod of testing: if anyone despises it he exposes himself to destruction, but if anyone turns back from his evil he is saved.

21.4.2.en: It is also observed that it is directed against the people as against all the princes of Israel who rejected his prophecy... He shows no partiality to an official at the expense of the individuals of the people, but all are equal before Him.

21.5.0.en: Finally, it stands at every gate, turning, striking right and left, so that none escapes it [15-16].

21.6.s.en: 3. The two ways of the king of Babylon:

21.6.0.en: 18 The word of the LORD came unto me again, saying, 19 "Also, thou son of man, appoint thee two ways, that the sword of the king of Babylon may come: both twain shall come forth out of one land: and choose thou a place, choose it at the head of the way to the city. 20 Appoint a way, that the sword may come to Rabbath of the Ammonites, and to Judah in Jerusalem the defenced. 21 For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination: he made his arrows bright, he consulted with images, he looked in the liver. 22 At his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem, to appoint captains, to open the mouth in the slaughter, to lift up the voice with shouting, to appoint battering rams against the gates, to cast a mount, and to build a fort. 23 And it shall be unto them as a false divination in their sight, to them that have sworn oaths: but he will call to remembrance the iniquity, that they may be taken. 24 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye have made your iniquity to be remembered, in that your transgressions are discovered, so that in all your doings your sins do appear; because, I say, that ye are come to remembrance, ye shall be taken with the hand.

21.6.1.en: It appears that the king of Babylon came to a meeting of two roads, one leading to Jerusalem and the other to Rabbah, the capital of the Ammonites, and here he began to consider which of them to attack first: Jerusalem or Rabbah. He used every pagan means: the sharpening of arrows to aim them down the two roads and cast lots, the inquiry of the teraphim, and the looking at the liver of the sacrifice that he offers to his god... and the answer came that he should begin with Jerusalem. In appearance the answer came through his evil pagan ways, but in reality it was God who secretly planned the discipline. The divination is false, but God, the Controller of all, turned the evil of the king and his divination to the discipline of the people.

21.6.2.en: It is observed that the Lord says: "Appoint a way, that the sword may come to... Judah in Jerusalem," since it appears that the majority of the people of Judah had crowded into the capital Jerusalem, thinking that even if all the cities of Judah fell, God would defend Jerusalem as "the city of the great King." But God affirms that she will receive the first strong blow, not only before all the cities of Judah but even before the cities of the Ammonites. Jerusalem, which knew much about God, deserved to be struck more, because she does not sin out of ignorance or lack of knowledge but in rebellion and disobedience.

21.7.0.en: 25 "And thou, profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day is come, when iniquity shall have an end, 26 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Remove the diadem, and take off the crown: this shall not be the same: exalt him that is low, and abase him that is high. 27 I will overturn, overturn, overturn, it: and it shall be no more, until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him.

21.7.1.en: God directs His speech directly against King Zedekiah, who destroys his people by his evil, saying: "And thou, profane wicked prince of Israel" [25]. The day has come to remove the turban and take the king's crown from him [26]. He thought himself great and destroyed his people; therefore the situation is reversed, and the king loses his crown forever: "I will overturn, overturn, overturn it" [27]. And He brings this arrogant king down to the depths, "until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him" [27]. The Lord Christ comes in His humility and reigns forever.

21.7.2.en: If the people of Zedekiah perished by the counsel of their king, the Lord of glory will reign and raise up His people and save them to reign with Him forever.

21.8.0.en: 28 "And thou, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning the Ammonites, and concerning their reproach; even say thou, The sword, the sword is drawn: for the slaughter it is furbished, to consume because of the glittering: 29 Whiles they see vanity unto thee, whiles they divine a lie unto thee, to bring thee upon the necks of them that are slain, of the wicked, whose day is come, when their iniquity shall have an end. 30 Shall I cause it to return into his sheath? I will judge thee in the place where thou wast created, in the land of thy nativity. 31 And I will pour out mine indignation upon thee, I will blow against thee in the fire of my wrath, and deliver thee into the hand of brutish men, and skilful to destroy. 32 Thou shalt be for fuel to the fire; thy blood shall be in the midst of the land; thou shalt be no more remembered: for I the LORD have spoken it."

21.8.1.en: The Ammonites escaped the sword of judgment because Nebuchadnezzar was occupied with Jerusalem, and they stood gloating.

21.8.2.en: The Ammonites reproached the people for their destruction and Jerusalem for its burning, but the discipline of Jerusalem is for a time, until the spiritual King arises and saves those who believe in Him, whereas the sword that shatters the Ammonites, which is the very same sword that shattered Judah, strikes not for discipline but for destruction, so that they are remembered no more.

21.8.3.en: The Ammonites did not enter into a covenant with God as Israel did, and yet they fell under the divine discipline, because God cannot bear sin either in the life of His people or in the life of others.

21.8.4.en: The Ammonites point to evil, not to the wicked: it is destroyed with a strong hand and does not rise again (Ammon was struck five years after Jerusalem).

21.8.5.en: The sword that destroys and executes!

21.8.6.en: * You used, my God, Nebuchadnezzar as a sword of destruction, and every heart melted, every hand grew slack, and all knees became as water!

21.8.7.en: You struck with the sword to separate in the heart between evil and good!

21.8.8.en: By the destroying sword You wanted repentance and returning to You!

21.8.9.en: * Before Your disciplines my soul trembles, and my whole being shakes!

21.8.10.en: As long as the sword is in Your hand, O Controller of all, O Lover of mankind, my soul is reassured and rests, O Receiver of sinners!

21.8.11.en: If You permit discipline, permit me repentance.

21.8.12.en: Convert me and I shall repent; heal me and I shall be healed!

21.8.13.en: * The Ammonites mocked Jerusalem and all Judah on the day of their discipline, but the very sword that disciplined Judah is the one that shattered Ammon!

21.8.14.en: Shatter Ammon within me, and discipline Jerusalem within me!

21.8.15.en: Scatter all evil within me, and sanctify Your work in me, O Giver of salvation and life!

21.8.16.en: I am reassured as long as the sword is in Your hand, O my Savior!

22.0.s.en: 1. A list of the sins of Judah:

22.0.0.en: 1 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Now, thou son of man, wilt thou judge, wilt thou judge the bloody city? yea, thou shalt shew her all her abominations. 3 Then say thou, Thus saith the Lord GOD, The city sheddeth blood in the midst of it, that her time may come, and maketh idols against herself to defile herself. 4 Thou art become guilty in thy blood that thou hast shed; and hast defiled thyself in thine idols which thou hast made; and thou hast caused thy days to draw near, and art come even unto thy years: therefore have I made thee a reproach unto the heathen, and a mocking to all countries. 5 Those that be near, and those that be far from thee, shall mock thee, which art infamous and much vexed. 6 Behold, the princes of Israel, every one were in thee to their power to shed blood. 7 In thee have they set light by father and mother: in the midst of thee have they dealt by oppression with the stranger: in thee have they vexed the fatherless and the widow. 8 Thou hast despised mine holy things, and hast profaned my sabbaths. 9 In thee are men that carry tales to shed blood: and in thee they eat upon the mountains: in the midst of thee they commit lewdness. 10 In thee have they discovered their fathers' nakedness: in thee have they humbled her that was set apart for pollution. 11 And one hath committed abomination with his neighbour's wife; and another hath lewdly defiled his daughter in law; and another in thee hath humbled his sister, his father's daughter. 12 In thee have they taken gifts to shed blood; thou hast taken usury and increase, and thou hast greedily gained of thy neighbours by extortion, and hast forgotten me, saith the Lord GOD. 13 "Behold, therefore I have smitten mine hand at thy dishonest gain which thou hast made, and at thy blood which hath been in the midst of thee. 14 Can thine heart endure, or can thine hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal with thee? I the LORD have spoken it, and will do it. 15 And I will scatter thee among the heathen, and disperse thee in the countries, and will consume thy filthiness out of thee. 16 And thou shalt be defiled by thyself in the sight of the heathen, and thou shalt know that I am the LORD."

22.1.0.en: The Lord gave a summary of the most hideous sins that the kingdom of Judah was committing at that time; and He concentrated them in two things: the shedding of blood and defilement with idols, so that He called Jerusalem the city that sheds blood [3], and infamous [5], instead of being the just, holy city.

22.1.1.en: A. She was called the city that sheds blood because she committed hideous crimes in which innocent blood was the victim, not in the narrow literal sense but in the wide sense. For this reason the Lord counted the dishonoring of parents, the oppression of the stranger, the vexing of the fatherless and the widow, and the taking of gifts and usury from the needy as crimes of shedding blood, because in them are the seizing of the rights of others and wronging them.

22.1.2.en: And the Christian, who sees the Lord Christ manifested in every person, counts every seizing of any of the rights of others as an insult directed to the Lord Christ Himself.

22.1.3.en: This is what the Lord Himself affirmed in His position on the great day of judgment, when He looks to those on His right hand saying: "Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me" (Mt 25:40), and to those on His left: "Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me" (Mt 25:45).

22.1.4.en: B. She was called "infamous," because she committed uncleannesses that offended God Himself, who is the Owner of the city, for it is "the city of the great King." The most important of these uncleannesses are the contempt for God's holy things and the profaning of His sabbaths, and the committing of adultery in its most hideous forms, such as adultery with forbidden female relatives (like the daughter-in-law or the sister) or a neighbour's wife or a wife in her menstruation...

22.2.s.en: 2. Judah condemned as dross in a fire:

22.2.0.en: 17 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 18 "Son of man, the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are even the dross of silver. 19 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye are all become dross, behold, therefore I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem. 20 As they gather silver, and brass, and iron, and lead, and tin, into the midst of the furnace, to blow the fire upon it, to melt it; so will I gather you in mine anger and in my fury, and I will leave you there, and melt you. 21 Yea, I will gather you, and blow upon you in the fire of my wrath, and ye shall be melted in the midst thereof. 22 As silver is melted in the midst of the furnace, so shall ye be melted in the midst thereof; and ye shall know that I the LORD have poured out my fury upon you."

22.2.1.en: Israel, before her division into two kingdoms (Israel and Judah), in the era of King David and his son Solomon, was like a shining head of gold, and after the division she became like two rods of silver; but when the two kingdoms turned aside to various pagan worships and were swept into the shedding of blood and abominations, they were changed into brass and tin and iron and lead... kinds of cheap and base metals, indeed they became dross, which, if put in the fire, is burned up. The fault is not in the fire but in the material exposed to the fire: if it is gold or silver it increases in purity and brightness, but if it is dross it is consumed and cast out.

22.3.0.en: In bitter reproach He says: "the house of Israel is to me become dross" [18], as though declaring that what they have become through their evil, they do not bear the consequences alone, but it offends God Himself, who acquired them and called His name upon them. Every sin we commit wounds the feelings of God Himself, because we are His children, and because of us His name is blasphemed by the nations.

22.4.s.en: 3. The prevalence of sin at every level:

22.4.0.en: 23 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 24 "Son of man, say unto her, Thou art the land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation. 25 There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey; they have devoured souls; they have taken the treasure and precious things; they have made her many widows in the midst thereof. 26 Her priests have violated my law, and have profaned mine holy things: they have put no difference between the holy and profane, neither have they shewed difference between the unclean and the clean, and have hid their eyes from my sabbaths, and I am profaned among them. 27 Her princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain. 28 And her prophets have daubed them with untempered morter, seeing vanity, and divining lies unto them, saying, Thus saith the Lord GOD, when the LORD hath not spoken. 29 The people of the land have used oppression, and exercised robbery, and have vexed the poor and needy: yea, they have oppressed the stranger wrongfully. 30 And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. 31 Therefore have I poured out mine indignation upon them; I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath: their own way have I recompensed upon their heads, saith the Lord GOD."

22.4.1.en: After presenting a list of the most hideous sins that Judah committed, so that she became dross to the Lord, He returned to affirm that this plague had come upon all: the prophets, the priests, the princes, and the people. The prophets became like lions, not to protect the people but to prey upon them and make their women widows. The priests, instead of presenting the divine commandment and sanctifying the people by pure, sincere worship, violated God's judgments and statutes and profaned His holy things, especially His sabbaths. The princes, instead of giving themselves for the people, cared for their material gain and became like ravening wolves that shed blood. As for the people, their nature became oppression and robbery.

22.5.0.en: It is observed that He does not say, "my prophets, my priests, the princes of my people, my people," but says, "her prophets, her priests, her princes, the people of the land" [25-28]. He does not want to attribute them to Himself in their evil, because they rejected Him and withdrew from Him, so He rejected them in order to discipline them and bring them back to Himself.

22.5.1.en: And He describes Jerusalem in all these ranks thus: "Thou art the land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation" [24]. For the Jews in all their classes rejected faith in Christ Jesus, the rain that comes down from heaven to cleanse the whole world and make of hearts a fruitful paradise... They became a land without cleansing, without rain, that is, without Christ; there is none to intercede for them in the day of wrath!

22.5.2.en: This reminds us of the sign that Gideon asked of God on the first night: "Behold, I will put a fleece of wool in the floor; and if the dew be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said" (Judg 6:37). The fleece pointed to the Jewish people, who alone among all the nations received the word of God in the Old Testament, so the fleece alone had the dew of water while all the earth was dry. As for the following night, which points to the New Testament, he asked the opposite, for there was dew on all the earth and dryness on the fleece of wool, a sign of the Jewish nation's rejection of the Lord Christ, the Word of God, or the heavenly dew, while the Gentile world accepted faith in Him. The Jewish nation became the land without rain!

22.6.0.en: Finally, having set forth the universality of sin at every level, God reproached them saying: "And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none" [30]. Who is this man who can build a wall or a hedge before the wrath of God and stand interceding for all mankind lest He destroy it?!

22.6.1.en: There is no being at all who is able to bear the wrath of God against the earth and intercede for it; therefore He sent His only-begotten Son as the Son of man. He alone can close this gap and stand bearing the divine wrath for us in His body, interceding for us by His pure blood and bringing us back to the Father's bosom.

22.6.2.en: In this St. Athanasius the Apostolic says:

22.6.3.en: [Since He is the Word of the Father and above all, He alone had the natural fitness to renew the creation of all things, to bear on behalf of all, and to be an intercessor for all before the Father.

22.6.4.en: "It was necessary that none other than God the Word Himself should become incarnate," for it became Him for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings (Heb 2:10). By these words he means that it was not the business of anyone else to bring men back from what they had begun, except the Word of God, who also made them from the beginning... for by the sacrifice of His body He put an end to the judgment that was against us].

22.6.5.en: What does it mean: "stand in the gap before me for the land" [30]?

22.6.6.en: The Son of man, the incarnate Word of God, stood in the gap, that is, in the chasm between the Father and men, to accomplish reconciliation between them (1 Tim 2:5). And we also, as we enjoy reconciliation with God, long to stand in the gap, to work and pray for every sinner, that he may meet his Savior and experience the same reconciliation that has become ours. Let each one of us be the man who stands in the gap before God, interceding and making every effort, desiring the salvation of every person. As the Apostle Paul says: "Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God" (2 Cor 5:20).

22.6.7.en: Here again he affirms the importance of prayer and intercession for others, for when God found none to intercede for His people, ruin came upon the people. He delivered Lot from the destroying fire because of the prayer of Abraham (Gen 19), and He delivered Israel from destruction by the prayer of Moses the prophet (Num 14:11-21), and Jerusalem was rescued from the hand of Sennacherib by the prayer of King Hezekiah (Isa 37:1-7, 34-36).

22.6.9.en: * My inner Jerusalem has become dross, so why do I blame the fire that consumed it?!

22.6.10.en: My unjust heart has become a shedder of the blood of the poor, and my defiled thoughts have profaned the Temple of the Lord within me; there has come to be a chasm between me and You, O God!

22.6.12.en: Who will stand in the gap before You to intercede for me, the chief of sinners?!

22.6.13.en: Who will pay my debt and renew my nature that I may meet You?

22.6.14.en: * I thank You, my Savior, O incarnate Word of God. You alone bore my sins; You alone were lifted up on the Cross; You turned my earth into heaven!

22.6.15.en: You gave me Your Holy Spirit working in me, and lifted my heart to the bosom of Your Father!

22.6.16.en: What of You, O wonderful and unique Intercessor?!

22.6.17.en: Grant me to love sinners and pray for them and be spent out of love for them!
